raw: 35.1 The Free Energy Principle and Predictive Processing[^106]
teaching_note: A generative model p specifies how latent states s could produce observations o; q is an approximate belief distribution over those states. With p and o fixed, reducing variational free energy over q improves posterior approximation within that model, not the truth of p; prediction error is not generally identical to free energy, and information-theoretic free energy is not a direct measure of physical energy use. The worked numeric example illustrates this distinction; the inherited thesis is secondary context, while the formal sources support the mathematical account. [@scholarly_friston_2010_fep; @scholarly_buckley_2017_fep_mathematical_review]
title: The Free Energy Principle and Predictive Processing

raw: 35.2 Active Inference as Computational Model of Intelligence Agent Behavior[^3]
teaching_note: Separate state inference from policy selection: a posterior describes beliefs under a model, epistemic policy value concerns expected information gain, and preference-related value concerns desired outcomes. Completed synthetic case: a fictional library page is unavailable; a model favors maintenance after reading a supplied maintenance notice, but a wrong-model alternative is that the notice describes a different library. Check the approved notice's identifier and date; if they mismatch, withdraw the model-based preference and abstain on cause rather than labeling the outage hostile or taking an action. These are proposed modeling choices, not evidence that an LLM implements active inference. [@scholarly_friston_2017_active_inference_process; @scholarly_dacosta_2020_discrete_active_inference]
title: Active Inference as Computational Model of Intelligence Agent Behavior

raw: 35.3 Shared Protentions in Multi-Agent Active Inference[^163]
teaching_note: The inherited term concerns shared anticipations of future states in a theoretical multi-agent account; the supplied source is commentary on research, not direct evidence that this curriculum's agents acquire them or coordinate without communication. A classroom analogy is two reviewers expecting the same checkpoint artifact, but agreement can arise from copied inputs rather than a validated shared model. Compare predicted handoff fields with the actual supplied record and retain disagreements; do not turn shared expectation into independent corroboration, permission or a human–agent equivalence.
title: Shared Protentions in Multi-Agent Active Inference

raw: 35.4 Active Inference for Social Organization and Intelligence Communities[^3]
teaching_note: Fox's paper relates active-inference constructs to industrial engineering and quality management, identifying repetitive work as a more natural fit than one-of-a-kind projects with changing conditions (abstract and Sections 1, 4–5). Its organizational analogy does not establish that an intelligence community has a single coherent generative model, that a modeled Markov blanket enforces access control, or that disagreement is dysfunction. Use a fictional recurring document-review process to specify expectations and nonconformances, while keeping plural goals and novel cases outside any claimed validation. [@ageint003]
title: Active Inference for Social Organization and Intelligence Communities

raw: 35.5 VERSES AI Research: Multi-Scale Active Inference Architectures[^163][^164]
teaching_note: Distinguish a multiscale architectural proposal, commentary about a paper and a vendor announcement of workshop participation. The inherited press release establishes an attributed announcement, not independent comparative accuracy, scalability, safety or product readiness; accepted papers are not a performance denominator. To assess a proposed hierarchy, require explicit state variables, cross-scale messages, baseline, tested task and failure cases; until those primary results are inspected, comparative efficacy remains unknown.
title: VERSES AI Research: Multi-Scale Active Inference Architectures

raw: 35.6 Cognitive Security Through the Active Inference Lens[^105]
teaching_note: The inherited cognitive-security ethics paper motivates concerns about automated influence; it does not validate an active-inference defense or a security guarantee for LLM agents. As a proposed analytic lens, distinguish a prior that filters out inconvenient evidence from a justified posterior update, and ask which independent observation could overturn the current interpretation. Surprise under a model is evidence of model–observation mismatch, not by itself manipulation, hostile intent or permission to intervene.
title: Cognitive Security Through the Active Inference Lens

raw: 35.7 Applications: Deception Detection, Surprise Minimization, Threat Modeling
teaching_note: The raw heading's 'deception detection' is an application hypothesis, not a demonstrated consequence of free-energy minimization; inherited STIX/TAXII/context citations do not supply that missing evidence. In the synthetic outage case, compare maintenance, publication error and an unexplained cause without inferring intent from an unexpected observation; if the approved packet cannot discriminate, stop at unresolved. Model-based information-seeking remains limited to authorized local records, and neither low free energy nor high posterior confidence confers authority. [@scholarly_dacosta_2020_discrete_active_inference]
title: Proposed applications: anomaly interpretation and bounded threat modeling

raw: 35.8 Applications of Active Inference and FEP in Intelligence (TU Delft Thesis)[^106]
teaching_note: The source-guide annotation identifies Sakarya's 2024 bachelor's literature review on modeling social human behavior, not an operational intelligence evaluation; preserve the original heading only as provenance. Separate the review's account of theory and model variants from any claim that those methods improve analytic accuracy, detect deception or scale to real-world tasks. A transfer claim needs an explicit implementation, relevant comparison and independently assessed outcomes; those are not supplied here, so operational benefit remains unknown.
title: TU Delft thesis: active-inference literature review and transfer limits
